flagged.evidence: Statement (5) asserts Neg(f) ⊆ N(w^{-1}) when w·f ∈ C. The current inversion-set definition gives N(q) = {α ∈ Φ₊ : ρ(q)α ∈ Φ₋}. In the scoped A₂ example, take w = st, g = (1,1), and f = (ts)·g = (1,-2); the displayed action gives w·f = g ∈ C. Then e_t ∈ Neg(f), but ρ(ts)e_t = e_s ∈ Φ₊, so e_t ∉ N(w^{-1}). Proof 1.1 also reverses the action in the equation g(ρ(w)^{-1}α) = f(α): from g = w·f the action formula gives g(ρ(w)α) = f(α), yielding N(w), not N(w^{-1}).

The page repeats the false bound Neg(f) ⊆ N(w^{-1}). The same scoped A₂ witness disproves it: w = st and f = (ts)·(1,1) = (1,-2) satisfy w·f ∈ C and e_t ∈ Neg(f), while ρ(ts)e_t = e_s ∈ Φ₊, so e_t ∉ N(w^{-1}).

The disk locator says `Lemmas D.3.1-D.2.5`. Davis's cited Appendix D.2 labels the relevant lemmas D.2.2–D.2.5, followed by Theorems D.2.6–D.2.7; the D.3.1–D.2.5 range is inaccurate. [Davis PDF](https://people.math.osu.edu/davis.12/davisbook.pdf)
